I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. The exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged. It type-checks under `tsc --strict`. I did not run a behaviour comparison against the original, because lodash isn't installed, so `src/module.ts` can't be bundled or run here.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 606 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of my own code. I couldn't get the size of the original for comparison, since the same command fails on `src/module.ts` without lodash.

- **`byId`:** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`, with `(row) => row.id` as before.
- **`totalAge`:** uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`. The `'age'` string shorthand isn't supported there, so I pass `(row) => row.age`. That is the only adapter.
- **`isBlank`:** uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main `es-toolkit` package has no `isEmpty` that handles all the input types, and the compat one follows lodash's rules. It returns `true` for `null`, booleans, numbers and empty strings, arrays and objects.

No lodash import remains.

I didn't try alternative `isEmpty` imports to see whether 606 bytes is the smallest reachable.
